newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Krasnoyarsk aluminium shakes up management.
newsitem.headline: Russian Krasnoyarsk aluminium shakes up management.

text.p: Russian aluminium smelter Krasnoyarsk, the world's second biggest, made a new shake-up of top management on Tuesday when it removed a recently appointed general director, who is an employee of Swiss trading house Glencore.
A Krasnoyarsk press release said Igor Vishnyevsky of Glencore AG had been replaced by former board chairman and current board member Gennady Druzhinin.
Druzhinin, speaking by telephone from the southern Siberian city of Krasnoyarsk, and Vishnyevsky, in Moscow, confirmed the changes.

Vishnyevsky was appointed two weeks ago to replace Igor Kolpakov, who resigned after the Interior Ministry said it was investigating allegations that Kolpakov might have mishandled funds. Kolpakov later told Reuters he had done nothing wrong and would clear his name.
Vishnyevsky is still president of Krazpa-Metals, a 50-50 joint venture between Krasnoyarsk and Glencore.
Krasnoyarsk accounted for 27 percent of Russia's total primary aluminium output last year of 2.87 million tonnes.
